newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - UK traded options market quiet, eye Dow.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - UK traded options market quiet, eye Dow.

text.p: The UK traded options market was quiet by midday on Monday with many investors still on the sidelines due to uncertainty as to the Dow's near-term direction after its record close last Friday, dealers said.
"The market is really dead. People are afraid that we could have a setback on Wall Street and don't want to get involved at the moment," one dealer said.
Trading volumes are likely to pick up on Tuesday ahead of Wednesday's expiration of January series individual stock options, he said.
The FTSE 100 index was up 42.2 at 4,099.0 by 1250 GMT.

The largest combination trade of the morning session was a strangle in Redland Plc. The strangle was set up when one dealer bought 1,000 March 300 puts at 8p and then bought 1,000 March 360 calls at 12p, for a total cost of 20p, plus commissions.
In this example, both options are out-of-the-money, with Redland shares trading at 334p, up 5-1/2p.

If Redland shares remain between 300p and 360p at the time of expiration, both options will expire worthless. A profit will be made, however, if Redland moves either above 360p or below 300p, with the potential profits quite large if the share moves a great deal before the March expiration.

Elsewhere, one dealer bought 1,000 June 110 calls at 4-1/2p to protect a sale of the underlying stock. By owning a call at the same time one is short, the risk is limited to a fixed and generally small amount.
If Tarmac falls in price by the June expiration, the dealer will make his profit on the short sale, less the 4-1/2p paid for the call, which will expire worthless.
